channel.title: AI Academy
channel.description: Learn AI, one chapter at a time. New chapter daily.

item.title: RLHF: Teaching AI with a Thumbs Up
item.description: Language models can write anything—including toxic nonsense. RLHF is the training technique that taught them what humans actually want.

item.title: Tokenization Quirks Every Developer Hits
item.description: Tokenization is the invisible first step in every LLM interaction. Its quirks explain some of AI's strangest failures—and knowing them makes you better.

item.title: How Training Actually Works
item.description: You know LLMs learn from data. But how, mechanically? Two passes through the network explain almost everything.

item.title: Reasoning Models: Thinking Before Answering
item.description: Standard LLMs blurt out answers. Reasoning models think first. Here's how that inner monologue works and why it matters.

item.title: The Case for Smaller, Smarter Models
item.description: Bigger isn't always better. Small language models are bringing real AI capabilities to phones, laptops, and robots — no cloud required.

item.title: Safety and Alignment: Where We Actually Stand
item.description: AI alignment isn't theoretical anymore—it's an engineering discipline with real progress and real gaps. Here's an honest snapshot of the current state.

item.title: The Electric Bill Behind Every Chatbot
item.description: Every AI response has a price tag. Here's what actually drives the cost of running LLMs in production and how companies try to shrink it.

item.title: Embeddings: How Machines Actually Understand Meaning
item.description: Embeddings turn words into coordinates in meaning-space. That simple idea powers the most useful AI search systems being built today.

item.title: Function Calling: How AI Learned to Use Tools
item.description: LLMs can't check your calendar or book a flight—unless you give them tools. Here's exactly how function calling works under the hood.

item.title: Open-Source vs Closed-Source Models in 2026
item.description: Open-source models have closed the quality gap. But the battle has shifted to new terrain: agents, tooling, and who controls the stack.

item.title: When AI Learned to See and Hear
item.description: Text-only AI was just the beginning. Multimodal models see photos, hear speech, and reason across all of it at once. Here's how they work.

item.title: Context Windows: Your AI's Short-Term Memory
item.description: Every AI model has a ceiling on how much text it can process at once. Understanding context windows changes how you use these tools.

item.title: Hallucinations: Why LLMs Make Things Up
item.description: LLMs don't retrieve facts. They predict plausible text. Understanding this distinction is the key to using them wisely.

item.title: Evals: How to Know If Your AI Actually Works
item.description: Everyone talks about building AI. Almost nobody talks about measuring it. Here's how evaluations work — and why they're the skill that separates toy demos from real systems.

item.title: Vector Databases: Where AI Stores Its Memories
item.description: Vector databases turn meaning into math so AI can find what's relevant. Here's what they do, why they matter, and when you need one.

item.title: Agentic AI: when the model uses tools
item.description: An LLM that can browse, code, and call APIs isn't a chatbot anymore. It's something new.

item.title: RAG vs fine-tuning vs just prompting
item.description: The three ways to make an LLM 'know' your data. Most people pick wrong.

item.title: Prompt engineering that actually works
item.description: Stop saying 'please'. Start giving structure, examples, and constraints. Here's how.

item.title: How LLMs actually work (without the math)
item.description: Tokens, weights, and attention — explained with everyday analogies, zero matrix equations.

item.title: What is AI, really?
item.description: Forget sci-fi. AI is pattern-matching at scale — and once you see it that way, the whole field clicks.
